claim: For every bandwidth \(a>0\) and every exponent \(s>\frac12\) with \(s\notin\{\frac32,\frac52,\frac72,\ldots\}\), set \(m=\lfloor s-\frac12\rfloor\) and let \(PW_a^s\) be the fractional Paley–Wiener reproducing-kernel Hilbert space of Monguzzi–Peloso–Salvatori. There is no countable real sequence \(\Lambda\subset\mathbb R\) and no constants \(0<A\le B<\infty\) such that \(A\|f\|_{PW_a^s}^2\le\sum_{\lambda\in\Lambda}|f(\lambda)|^2\le B\|f\|_{PW_a^s}^2\) for every \(f\in PW_a^s\).

integrity.computational_evidence: No numerical computation or finite enumeration is used.
integrity.proof_basis: Kernel-frame reduction, Taylor remainder estimates, integrability at zero and infinity, Bessel-sequence properties, and compactness contradiction.

scientific_limitations: Applies only to s > 1/2 with s not in {3/2, 5/2, 7/2, ...}.
Excludes critical half-integer exponents because the cited source does not define those cases in the same way.
Concerns real point samples of f itself, not complex sampling points or samples of the fractional Laplacian.
title: No real sampling sequences in supercritical fractional Paley–Wiener spaces
